description:
## Goal
Introduce a small Jido.AI.Backend execution/model boundary so Jido.AI can use ReqLLM, local Nx/Serving, or another implementation. ReqLLM remains the zero-configuration default. This epic records the implementation plan; implementing an Nx adapter, model loading, and serving supervision are outside scope.

## Agreed shared-data contract (explicit user decision)
ReqLLM.Response is the shared generation response contract for ALL Jido.AI backends, including local inference. Its namespace identifies the package defining the data structure, NOT the backend that executed the request. Constructing it does not require invoking ReqLLM generation, transport, provider, or model-resolution functions. Explicitly document this in the behavior and backend-author guide. Do not introduce Backend.Response. Shared messages, contexts, tools, tool calls, content parts, and stream chunks may remain ReqLLM types; adapters translate native representations.

## Compatibility requirements
Preserve zero-configuration operation, existing generation response structs, action results, signals, errors, aliases and ReqLLM model-input forms, HTTP/provider/generation options, tool loops, repair policy, WebSocket reuse, continuation, and compatible existing checkpoints. Existing stream_text/2 returns native ReqLLM.StreamResponse by default; add stream_format: :backend for a portable handle. All internal consumers use the portable handle.

## Architecture
Introduce Jido.AI.Backend (behavior/dispatch), Backend.Ref (module/options), Backend.ModelInfo, Backend.Stream, Backend.Embedding, and Backends.ReqLLM. Use Zoi-first schemas for Jido-owned structures. Required model callbacks: resolve_model/2 and model_info/2. Optional execution callbacks: generate/3, stream/3, generate_object/4, embed/3; require at least one supported execution operation. Generation/object callbacks return ReqLLM.Response, streaming returns Backend.Stream, embeddings return Backend.Embedding. capabilities is derived from model_info. Optional normalize_options(operation, model, opts), and paired open_session/1 + close_session/1 hooks. Missing operations and invalid results produce structured errors. Separate generation options, backend configuration, and reserved execution/session context. Strip internal keys before ReqLLM calls.

## Selection and model rules
Precedence: explicit request/action > agent/runtime/plugin defaults > application configuration > ReqLLM. Resolve once per run and carry Backend.Ref explicitly across async boundaries. Same-backend options merge shallowly; changing backend discards inherited options from the previous module. No global mutation or process-dictionary selection. Atom inputs retain Jido alias meaning; alias lookup precedes backend validation. Custom model references must never reach ReqLLM.model or LLMDB. Per-turn transformers can change models within the fixed selected backend; normalize options after the model override. A local backend must be configured with appropriate models rather than reinterpreting remote default aliases.

## Ownership
Jido owns conversation construction, tools, validation/repair policy, orchestration/deadlines, signals, telemetry and checkpoints. Backends own inference/transport, model/provider discovery, native adaptation, request option validation, cancellation/resource cleanup, provider sessions and provider continuation options. Shared pure data/schema helpers remain allowed outside adapters; executable provider integration does not.

## Results, streaming and metadata
Document response fields id/model/message/context/object/finish_reason/usage/provider_meta/error, stable tool-call IDs and reasoning/multimodal fidelity. Do not fabricate unavailable usage/costs. Embedding result is ordered batch vectors with model, dimensions and optional usage/metadata; retain existing public embedding shapes via translation. Stream contains consume/cancel/idempotent-close functions and optional native value. Consumption delivers ordered ReqLLM.StreamChunk callbacks and returns final ReqLLM.Response or tagged error. Cover single-consumer semantics, final usage/finish reason, partial failures, blocked cancellation, early halt, callback exceptions and owner death; try/after alone cannot handle forced termination. Distinguish stopping delivery from interrupting local computation. ModelInfo includes stable identity/label/reference, capabilities/modalities/tools/structured mode/reasoning, limits, dimensions and optional pricing/metadata. Unknown is not false or zero; metadata must not trigger inference/model loading.

## Runtime completeness
Audit and migrate facades, all actions/helpers, directives, plugins/defaults, agent/request/signal schemas, strategy allowlists/configuration and CLI forwarding, child workers, all tool-followup calls, output repair, and ReAct including StreamResponse processing. CoT worker directly reads stream_response.stream and usage and must migrate too. Remove OpenAI/OpenAICodex detection/session creation/provider-option injection/previous_response_id translation/cleanup from ReActRunner. Runtime owns only opaque sessions and generic continuation bookkeeping. Bind continuation to backend/model identity; never reuse across incompatible model changes.

## Checkpoints and observability
New compatibility data includes backend and stable model/deployment identity, never credentials/live handles/PIDs/functions. Legacy checkpoints are accepted only for compatible ReqLLM configuration; preserve response-ID continuation through a compatibility mapping and recreate resources on resume. Add backend telemetry identity without changing existing event names/result shapes. Preserve ReqLLM errors and existing sanitization; use existing Jido.AI.Error conventions for new boundary errors.

## Delivery sequence
1 Characterization; 2 contracts/dispatch; 3 ReqLLM adapter; 4 facades/actions/directives; 5 configuration/strategy propagation; 6 ReAct sessions/streams/repair; 7 integration/isolation/checkpoint verification; 8 documentation.

```mermaid
graph LR
  S1[1 Characterization] --> S2[2 Contracts and dispatch]
  S2 --> S3[3 ReqLLM adapter]
  S3 --> S4[4 Facades actions directives]
  S4 --> S5[5 Runtime propagation]
  S5 --> S6[6 ReAct and repair]
  S6 --> S7[7 Verification]
  S7 --> S8[8 Documentation]
```

## Definition of done
A deterministic custom backend completes model resolution, streaming, tool loops and structured-output repair without any ReqLLM execution/model-resolution calls. Concurrent backends are isolated. Existing default behavior and public contracts remain compatible. Architectural tests prevent leaks and backend authors have explicit shared-data/lifecycle specifications. Final checks: mix precommit, full stable mix test, Credo, Dialyzer, mix docs and affected examples/scripts. Do not edit CHANGELOG.md (release notes are generated).

## Research basis
Plan was developed against the earlier checkout and must be reconciled with current HEAD during characterization; current prime reports main at 17c10b55 with uncommitted user changes. Do not overwrite those changes. This recording step does not start implementation.
